# Scientist Playbook — GPU cloud rental price forecaster (stage PACK_ONLY)

<!-- LAB-PROTECTED:BEGIN (owned by the lab; rewrites cannot remove or edit this block) -->
## Lab rules (protected)
- The lab, not you, decides when research stops. "Accept/freeze the champion" is never a valid plan: every
  iteration must test a real, falsifiable change. A string of reverts means the explored families are exhausted,
  not that the problem is solved; move to an untried family (see the experiment registry) or make a bolder change.
- Every hypothesis is tagged with one family and a novelty (incremental | bold). Do not spend more than two
  consecutive experiments in one family without a promotion; after two reverts in a row, the next one is bold.
- Near-misses are archived with their code, diff and diagnostics (inspect_candidate) and can be built on, but a
  near-miss of the same model class is a local move. A small Holdout gain is not "confirmed": Holdout has 5 origins
  and per-candidate deltas of +-0.002 are noise. Do not stack levers by their Holdout deltas.
- Every candidate is tagged with a model_class (see the lab's list). When the lab directive says MODEL-CLASS
  EXPLORATION, write a forecaster of a different class for the AWS regime from scratch (write_candidate), compare
  several classes on Discovery (save_variant / load_variant) and submit the best one.
- One failed implementation falsifies that implementation, not the idea. Only mark a lever or class "dead" after
  two independent implementations fail (an implementation bug, e.g. an exploding quantile, falsifies nothing).
- A candidate whose Holdout aggregates equal the champion's (NO_OP) changed nothing that is scored: its
  selection rule never fired. Make changes that act unconditionally or show on Discovery that they fire.
- Guardrails are only removed with evidence: cite the iteration that falsified them in the rationale.
- Keep this playbook a distilled strategy (heuristics, guardrails, ranked ideas). The full experiment history
  is rendered by the lab from the ledger; do not copy the notebook into the playbook.
<!-- LAB-PROTECTED:END -->

## Mission
Beat the champion on the four Holdout gates (pooled skill, breadth, calibrated 80% band, no bad horizon) with forecasts that would also be honest at the frozen 2026-11-06 origin.

## Current champion state (episode start: PACK_ONLY iteration 8, PROMOTED)
Discovery pooled 0.4462, median 0.2831, coverage 0.7947. Holdout pooled 0.3088, median 0.2745, coverage 0.7514, horizons 0.4030/0.3369/0.2801. Gate-1 threshold: holdout pooled > 0.3118. Champion class: pooled_linear_momentum (regime A: pooled OLS momentum + vol-window ensemble {7,14,28} at h3/h7 + 0.95 h1 tail narrowing + vol-scaled conformal z; regimes B/C empirical change quantiles).
**Episode comparison bar:** the frozen v000 episode from this same champion locked the 50/50 GBM x pooled-linear-momentum blend at Discovery pooled 0.4814 (delta +0.0352; holdout PROMOTED: pooled 0.3412, median 0.2960, coverage 0.7493). A lock this episode beats it only if Discovery pooled > ~0.4824 (delta > +0.0362). No within-champion-class lever has ever moved holdout pooled more than +0.012 — the bar is reachable only through the tree member (solo GBM: Discovery 0.4856), a better blend weight, or a new class.

## Where the loss lives (check before every hypothesis)
~95% of champion loss is AWS hyperscaler_spot (h7 ~63%, h3 ~27%, h1 ~10%); one exploding cell annihilates the pooled score — read `slices[].share_of_total_loss` and `worst_series` first. Read `mean_q50_error`/`bias_rel` vs `mean_width_rel` before choosing a lever: most "width" problems are centering problems (iter-10: the GBM's under-coverage was centering-driven; after the center fix it covered 0.789 vs 0.761).

## Method
1. Diagnose from Discovery only: per-slice skill, breach asymmetry, worst series (bias vs width).
2. State ONE falsifiable hypothesis with a mechanism and a predicted sign.
3. Change one thing at a time so the ledger attributes the effect; when stacking CONFIRMED levers, attribute via per-lever deltas already measured on Holdout.
4. Record results, including negative results and their magnitude. Use analyze_discovery to measure out-of-sample BEFORE spending a dry run or a submission (budget: ~6 analyses, 8 dry runs per iteration).
5. **Dry-run budget is precious: a crashed dry run still consumes one.** Iter 10 lost its last dry run to a trivial unpack bug and then the Holdout submission CRASHED on the same bug class (4-tuple unpacked as 5) — nothing was evaluated. Before ANY dry run or submission: re-read the changed lines, check every tuple unpack against the actual arity, prefer indexing (`t[0]`, `t[1]`) over starred/unpack patterns.
6. **In-sample Discovery diagnostics LIE about the median when a lever widens bands** (PACK_ONLY 8: in-sample -0.0146, holdout +0.0193) **and about centering** (the champion's center is in-sample-optimal by construction, so ANY centering shift is in-sample-negative, ~4x its OOS gain). A centering lever can only pass the pre-Holdout screen bundled with an in-sample-positive lever of at least the same size.
7. Slice-level dry-run deltas catch width leaks that aggregate pooled skill hides: read `slice_deltas_best_first` for exact zeros / unexpected signs before submitting; also use dry runs to DECOMPOSE a stack lever-by-lever.
8. **LOCK-SELECTION RULE (how to pick the variant to submit).** Rank all screen-passing variants by **Discovery pooled skill** — the episode's comparison metric — and lock the top-ranked variant that passes a single OOS veto on a dense pseudo-origin backtest: (a) OOS pooled delta > 0 AND (b) OOS median >= the Gate-2 floor equivalent. NEVER select a variant for OOS-median parity or minimal gate margin: in g001_candidate the parity choice (w_gbm=0.35, OOS median exactly at champion parity) cost 0.0083 Discovery pooled vs w=0.50 and lost the episode comparison, while the "riskier" w=0.50 passed every holdout gate with margin (median 0.2960 vs floor 0.2695). Before locking any blend, sweep its member-dominance axis with dry runs (e.g. w_gbm in {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}; the measured curve is monotone: w=0.5 -> 0.4814, w=1.0 plain GBM -> 0.4856). If the top-pooled variant fails the OOS median veto, spend ONE lever on median repair — shrink the drifting tree member's q50 toward the LINEAR member's q50 (still untested: iter-10's shrink runs were invalidated by the center-inflation bug) — rather than down-weighting the better-pooled member.

## HARD guardrails (measured; cite the falsifying iteration to remove any)
- **EXA web search IS usable** (PACK_PLUS_EXA 4, PROMOTED): fixed few queries, point-in-time age-gated, fallback-safe (multiplier 1.0 = champion), pre-screened OOS; hardware_fundamentals/capability_ladder unusable for level anchoring. (PACK_ONLY has no external_signals.)
- **Bound every output:** clip per-series z to a small multiple of pooled z AND clip log-quantiles to +/- 1 of log last; `lv` is ALREADY a log value — never np.log it (iter-10 analog bug: bounds collapsed to exp(-12.8), REJECTED_SANITY).
- **Re-assign per-horizon quantities (z, beta) inside the horizon loop BEFORE any conditional override (PACK_PLUS_EXA 2). Never touch the LOWER quantile with a "max"** (PACK_ONLY 3): max raises q10, narrowing the lower band; upper-tail widening must leave z10 byte-identical.
- **Recent-window residuals do NOT estimate forward tails (falsified 3x):** state/conditioned width levers dead; unconditional smoothing (ensemble averaging) is the one width lever that WORKS (PACK_ONLY 8, 9); 270-day z window CONFIRMED at h1, FALSIFIED at h3 (PACK_PLUS_EXA 2).
- **Dead levers (do not retry):** chained-residual z at h3/h7 (PACK_PLUS_EXA 3); fixed-factor q90-only widening in ALL forms (PACK_ONLY 3, 5; PACK_PLUS_EXA 1); per-instance-type hierarchy (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5); h7 tail-factor frontier EXHAUSTED at 0.95, h3 stays 0.95 (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5); ensemble with a drift/persistence member (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5); marketplace band widening, OOS loss-negative at every origin (PACK_PLUS_EXA 4); per-series local calibration, catastrophic (PACK_ONLY 2); per-series conditional width rules (PACK_ONLY 7); momentum-beta shrinkage toward zero (PACK_ONLY 4, 7); in-sample mean drift (PACK_ONLY 5, 7); cross-collector pull / cross-AZ consensus (PACK_ONLY 1); calm-regime z narrowing, long-lag momentum, regime-B/C centering variants, aggregator_medians/index_prints, richer vol-window member sets (iters 5-9, PACK_PLUS_EXA 2).
- **Validation-selected changes that can also select "no change" degenerate to the champion on holdout** (PACK_ONLY 4): a lever needing a gain must act unconditionally or show on Discovery that its rule fires. **Ensemble across perturbed hyperparameters of the SAME model is CONFIRMED-POSITIVE (PACK_ONLY 8, 9).**
- **Center arithmetic in log-change space:** `q50_new = shrink * q50_old` scales the deviation from persistence; `q50_old + shrink*q50_old` DOUBLES the center at shrink=1.0 (iter-10 bug). Hand-check the arithmetic on a concrete number before running.
- Pool parameters across series with short histories (< 60 days); point-in-time only (rows dated on or before the origin; never hard-code dates or per-origin constants).
- Code: numpy/pandas/sklearn, vectorised, < 20 s/origin (GBM ~7 s); guard empty histories/NaNs; return every target series; enforce q10 <= q50 <= q90 and positivity; double-check lag indexing on a hand-computed example (iter-1: t+1-vs-t-1 -> skill -1e7; iter 3: level-vs-change mix -> coverage 0.13); **check series start dates before designing pseudo-origin protocols** (PACK_PLUS_EXA 5: card series start 2026-08-04, ~51 rows — early pseudo-origins scored zero cells, ZeroDivisionError masqueraded as a zero-loss frontier).

## MODEL-CLASS EXPLORATION results (iteration 10, PACK_ONLY)
- **gradient_boosting** (HistGradientBoostingRegressor loss='quantile', features = 1/3/7-day log changes + 7/14/28-day local vol, pooled over AWS, 540-day train): **Discovery pooled 0.4856 vs champion 0.4462 (+0.039, 10/11 origins)** — the largest single-model gain measured here; NONLINEARITY of the state->change map was the binding constraint. BUT median 0.2438 vs 0.2831 (-0.039, tree q50 drifts on calm sticky zones) — Gate-2 risk.
- **analog_nonparametric:** Discovery pooled 0.4264 (-0.020, screen FAIL) despite median +0.020 — negative in this form; a second independent implementation needed to call the class dead.
- **model_combination** (log-space quantile average GBM x pooled-linear-momentum): the fixed 50/50 blend measured Discovery pooled 0.4814 (+0.0352, screen PASS) and was PROMOTED on Holdout (pooled 0.3412, median 0.2960, coverage 0.7493) — the biggest holdout promotion in this lab. The weight curve on Discovery is monotone toward the tree: w=0.35 -> 0.4731, w=0.50 -> 0.4814, w=1.0 -> 0.4856; w=0.7 backtested at OOS pooled +0.0459 but OOS median 0.2666 (below the Gate-2 floor) — the region w in (0.5, 1.0) is otherwise UNMEASURED on Discovery.
- GBM under-coverage (q90 breach 14-17% at h3/h7) is centering-driven: symmetric tail widening after the center fix (gbm_wide3: 0.4808 pooled / 0.7886 cov) was slightly WORSE than the plain GBM — widening is unnecessary once the center is correct.
- Untried classes: quantile_regression, state_space, volatility_model, regime_switching, hierarchical_pooling. Untried families: cross_series, exogenous_signals, robustness.

## Ranked untried directions (next lock must beat Discovery pooled ~0.4824; next promotion needs holdout pooled > 0.3412 + margin)
1. **Blend weight sweep + lock selection under Method step 8 (highest priority):** dry-run w_gbm in {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} on Discovery (curve monotone between endpoints 0.4814 and 0.4856), backtest the top-pooled variants on dense pseudo-origins, apply the OOS veto, lock the winner. If the top-pooled variant fails the OOS median veto, test the ONE median-repair lever: shrink the tree member's q50 toward the LINEAR member's q50 (untested; iter-10's shrink runs were invalidated by the center-inflation bug — hand-check the arithmetic per the guardrail).
2. **GBM member refinement:** richer features (lagged vol ratios, day-since-last-change for sticky zones), a third blend member (the champion's vol-scaled conformal z), or a per-series conformal layer on the GBM — could push the blend past the solo GBM's 0.4856.
3. **New classes (untried):** quantile_regression (linear/spline per horizon — the natural non-tree alternative); state_space / volatility_model (local-level Kalman or EWMA-vol band — likely a blend member); cross_series in pooled/cross-sectional form only (per-instance-type hierarchy falsified, PACK_PLUS_EXA 5).

## Notebook (key entries; full history rendered by the lab)
- Iters 0-9: champion is iter 8 (vol-window ensemble at h3/h7, holdout 0.3088).
- Iter 10: model-class exploration crashed on a tuple-unpack bug; the gradient_boosting member measured Discovery pooled 0.4856 (screen PASS, median -0.039 Gate-2 risk); analog_nonparametric 0.4264 (screen FAIL).
- Iter 11 (PROMOTED): the fixed GBM x linear 50/50 blend was locked at w=0.50 (Discovery 0.4814; holdout pooled 0.3412, median 0.2960, coverage 0.7493). Lesson recorded in Method step 8: parity/conservative weight selection (w=0.35) sacrificed Discovery pooled without being needed for the gates. The region w in (0.5, 1.0) remains unmeasured on Discovery; the tree-q50-toward-linear-q50 shrink is untested.

# Improver policy (I_g, improver component)

Read the released research episodes and measured results. Identify one repeated failure in the forecasting or research
procedure (for example: experiments that never left one model class, diagnostics run in an unhelpful order, evidence
searched without a testable question, hypotheses without a rejection condition, Discovery gains that did not survive
Holdout). Propose ONE bounded change, explain the behavior it should alter, and specify a comparison that could reject
it. You may revise the researcher instructions (research_policy) or these improver instructions (improver_policy).
Cite the episode ids that support the change. Never claim the change is proved: the lab runs the comparison.

revision.change: Add ONE new Method step 8, a LOCK-SELECTION RULE: when several variants pass the Discovery screen, rank them by DISCOVERY POOLED SKILL (the episode's comparison metric) subject to a single OOS veto (dense pseudo-origin backtest: pooled delta > 0 AND OOS median >= the Gate-2 floor), and lock the top-ranked variant. Selecting a variant for OOS-median parity or minimal gate margin is prohibited (g001_candidate: the parity choice w=0.35 cost 0.0083 Discovery pooled vs w=0.50 and lost the episode comparison, while the 'riskier' w=0.50 passed every holdout gate with margin, median 0.2960 vs floor 0.2695). The rule further requires sweeping the blend's member-dominance axis with dry runs (w_gbm in {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}; the measured curve is monotone: w=0.5 -> 0.4814, w=1.0 plain GBM -> 0.4856), and if the top-pooled variant fails the OOS median veto, spending ONE median-repair lever (shrink the drifting tree q50 toward the LINEAR member's q50 — never actually tested; iter-10's shrink runs were invalidated by the center-inflation bug) instead of down-weighting the better-pooled member. Champion state and notebook updated with the episode comparison bar (frozen lock 0.4814; a winning lock needs Discovery pooled > ~0.4824) and iter 11.
revision.expected_behavior_change: The next episode, instead of stopping at the 50/50 resubmission (Discovery 0.4814, the frozen episode's lock) or choosing a conservative parity weight (0.4731, the v001 episode's losing lock), spends its dry runs sweeping w_gbm in {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} on Discovery, backtests the top-pooled variants on dense pseudo-origins, applies the OOS veto, tests the tree-q50-toward-linear-q50 median repair if needed, and locks the highest Discovery-pooled veto-passing variant — expected lock at Discovery pooled >= ~0.484, above the frozen bar of 0.4824.
revision.development_comparison: Same champion (pooled_linear_momentum iter 8, Discovery pooled 0.4462) and same budget. Compare the Discovery pooled delta of the forecaster locked under the revised policy against the frozen v000 episode's lock (delta +0.0352, skill 0.4814); the revision is developed only if the new lock's delta exceeds +0.0362. Observable procedural differences to log: dry runs spent on the weight axis before lock, the locked w_gbm (expected > 0.5 vs frozen 0.5), and whether a median-repair lever was tested before any fallback.
revision.rejection_condition: Rejected if the episode under the revised policy locks nothing, fails the screen, or locks a forecaster with Discovery pooled delta <= +0.0362 (does not beat the frozen lock 0.4814 by the 0.001 margin) — including the case where the weight sweep finds no veto-passing variant above 0.4824 and the rule merely consumed dry-run budget before falling back to w=0.5. Also rejected if the OOS-veto rule causes a lock that fails the screen or crashes unevaluated.
